text:
Wesley Fofana, as a former Leicester City player, might have expected the celebrating Nottingham Forest fans to give him a hard time. But, at the end of a week in which he invited opprobrium by making light of missing a penalty at Liverpool in an unsanctioned French interview, he endured the ultimate ignominy when Chelsea supporters chanted foul-mouthed abuse at him, concluding: “You’re not welcome here.”
Fofana was humiliated by Liam Delap before fouling the former Chelsea striker to allow Morgan Gibbs-White to score a penalty for the first of his two goals that ultimately allowed Forest to follow their win over Manchester City to climb to 14th in the Premier League.
But even two goals for substitute Emmanuel Emegha, following on from his effort against Leeds, could not allow Xabi Alonso to smile after this fourth defeat in five games. There is clearly something rotten at the heart of Chelsea.
With the rain, fog and cold, an uncomfortable Friday night out in Nottingham soon became even more inhospitable for Chelsea. A rumbustious atmosphere was heightened when Forest went ahead with their first clear attack inside five minutes.
Liam Delap, with more than a point to prove, had already had one speculative 20-yarder on the turn saved by Emiliano Martínez after 62 seconds. Yet Chelsea, continuing their horrendous week, failed to heed the warning. When Jair Cunha nudged the ball wide to Daniel Muñoz, the right wing-back was given as much space to cross the ball as Igor Jesus was to swivel and plant his delicious right-foot volley into the top corner. It was a sumptuous goal, from the striker who also scored in Forest’s 3-1 win at Stamford Bridge in May, but the freedom he was given by the Chelsea defenders was baffling.
Xabi Alonso had elected to retain Fofana, despite the defender’s outrageously loose comments to a French YouTuber this week, and drop Levi Colwill, Moisés Caicedo retreating to the centre-back berth he adopted at Sunderland in emergency recently. With Forest bound to look to the physicality of Delap, it seemed a strange decision.
Andrew Madley, the referee, added flavour to this concoction by allowing Morgan Gibbs-White to shove Fofana off the ball with impunity, earning Forest a corner, then Caicedo to push Delap to the ground, again keeping the pea in his whistle dry. Chelsea gradually worked their way back into the game but without threatening more than a deflected shot from Roméo Lavia in the first half.
Forest were content to revert to a flat back five and ask Gibbs-White and Igor Jesus to work off Delap. Yet Chelsea, for all Alonso’s repeated insistence that he wants his team to press high, continuously allowed midfielders James McAtee and Xaver Schlager to have the ball as they came over halfway. It is not surprising to hear 15 teams came into this weekend having allowed opponents fewer passes per defensive action when observing this Chelsea showing.
Fofana’s decision to laugh at his shootout penalty miss in the EFL Cup defeat at Liverpool, and admit he had to be talked out of giving up football by his agent, in his unsanctioned interview this week has only worsened relations between Chelsea and their supporters. But then three defeats in their previous four Premier League games doesn’t exactly help. And playing with their precise, careful and blunt approach of the opening 45 minutes could have put the tin hat on things.
The night became even more embarrassing for Chelsea, and Fofana in particular, inside the first five minutes – again – of kick-off. The France defender misjudged a straightforward channel ball from James McAtee so that Delap got away from him. The former Chelsea striker knew he just had to get ahead of his man and either he would be able to get his shot away or his heels would be clipped. Fofana duly obliged; Gibbs-White converted the penalty.
The Chelsea fans in the Bridgford Stand compounded their player’s nightmare week with their abusive chants. Delap span away from his man with ease, Fofana knowing he could not risk fouling him from behind again. When Colwill, the substitute, prepared to come on, Chelsea’s No 3 had walked to the touchline before his number had even flashed up on the digital board. His humiliation was complete.
To the surprise of most in the ground, Chelsea came back into the game within three minutes of Gibbs-White’s penalty. Pedro Neto, who at least played with heart, surged across on to a one-two with Morgan Rogers to fire a shot goalwards that deflected off Cunha and fell for Emegha, on as a half-time substitute for Danny Welbeck, to score from close range. After his goal on his full Premier League debut against Leeds last week, perhaps this was something for Chelsea to build on.
The hope did not last long, however. Rogers, uncharacteristically, slashed wide when left free from Jordan Henderson’s corner. And when Gibbs-White timed his run on to Schlager’s brilliantly inventive pass to dink his third goal of the season over Martínez, Forest’s second successive home win looked assured. Chelsea’s dignity had long since been misplaced.

נוטינגהאם פורסט גברה על צ'לסי בתוצאה 3-2 הודות ליכולת גבוהה של מורגן גיבס-וייט, שכבש צמד שערים, ושל איגור ז'ז'וס שהבקיע שער מוקדם. המשחק הותיר את צ'לסי בהפסד נוסף ובמצב מקצועי רע מאוד תחת הדרכתו של צ'אבי אלונסו.

המשחק התאפיין באווירה קשה עבור צ'לסי, כאשר המגן ווסלי פופานה ספג קריאות בוז קשות מהאוהדים על רקע התנהלותו מחוץ למגרש. למרות ניסיונות קאמבק של האורחים ושערים של המחליפים, פורסט שמרה על היתרון והבטיחה לעצמה את הניצחון.
